description: Graphical front ends for ULPs: the predefined dialogs (dlgDirectory, dlgFileOpen/dlgFileSave, dlgMessageBox), all dialog objects from dlgCell to dlgVBoxLayout, layout rules, the dialog functions dlgAccept, dlgRedisplay, dlgReset, dlgReject and dlgSelectionChanged, the escape character, a complete example and the supported HTML subset. Dialogs require the interactive editor. Source: EAGLE 9.6.0 built-in help.

tools.name: dlgDirectory
tools.description: Shows a standard directory selection dialog and returns the full path of the chosen directory, or an empty string if the user cancels. An optional start directory sets where browsing begins.
tools.notes: Always handle the empty result (cancel).

tools.name: dlgFileOpen, dlgFileSave
tools.description: Show the standard file dialogs for opening or saving a file and return the full path of the selected file, or an empty string on cancel. An optional start path and a filter restrict the listed files; the filter can be a wildcard, a list of wildcards or descriptive text, with several file types separated by ';;'.
tools.usage:
string dlgFileOpen(string Title[, string Start[, string Filter]])
string dlgFileSave(string Title[, string Start[, string Filter]])
tools.notes: With an empty Start the current directory is used; with an empty Filter all files are shown. The dialogs only return a name - reading or writing is done with fileread()/output(). Writing .brd/.sch/.lbr names via output() needs mode "F".

tools.name: dlgMessageBox
tools.description: Shows a modal message box with up to three buttons and returns the index of the button pressed (0 for the first). The first button is the default (Enter) and the last one the cancel button (Esc or closing the box), unless others are marked with '+' or '-'. A leading ';', '!' or ':' in the message adds an information, warning or error icon; the message may contain HTML.
tools.usage:
int dlgMessageBox(string Message[, button_list])
Message prefixes: ';' information   '!' warning   ':' error
button_list: up to 3 strings, e.g. "&Yes", "&No", "-Cancel" (default: "OK")

parameters.name: Message
parameters.description: Text (optionally HTML) with an optional icon prefix.

parameters.name: button_list
parameters.description: Comma-separated button texts; '+' marks the default, '-' the cancel button, '&' a hotkey.

tools.notes: In HTML messages write < > & for literal <, > and &. To start a message or button text with a literal ';', '!', ':', '+' or '-' escape it. On macOS only ':' shows an icon. For a quick non-modal note use status().

tools.name: dlgDialog
tools.description: Executes a user-defined dialog: the block contains dialog objects (and optionally ordinary statements that decide which objects to add) and the call returns when the dialog is closed. The return value is the value passed to dlgAccept() or dlgReject(), or -1 if the window is simply closed. It is the only dialog object that is a real function, so it can be used wherever a function call is allowed.

parameters.name: block
parameters.description: Dialog objects and statements in braces.

tools.notes: Note the semicolon after the closing brace. The dialog contains a dlgVBoxLayout by default. Always provide a button that calls dlgAccept() (and a cancel button calling dlgReject()) so the user can close it properly. A dialog waits for the user, so ULPs meant to run unattended (e.g. from a script) should skip it, for example when an argv option is given.

tools.name: dlgCell
tools.description: Places a dialog object into a cell of a dlgGridLayout, addressed by row and column (starting at 0), or makes it span a range of cells when a second row/column pair is given. A cell contains a dlgHBoxLayout by default, so several objects in one cell are arranged side by side.
tools.usage: dlgCell(int row, int column[, int row2, int column2]) statement
tools.notes: Only valid directly inside a dlgGridLayout.

tools.name: dlgCheckBox
tools.description: Defines a check box with a label bound to an int variable: the variable is 1 while checked and 0 otherwise, and its initial value sets the initial state. An optional statement runs each time the box is toggled.
tools.notes: Every check box in a dialog needs its own variable. If the text contains '&', the next character becomes an Alt hotkey; write \\& in the ULP source for a literal '&'.

tools.name: dlgComboBox
tools.description: Defines a drop-down selection field filled from a string array; the int variable holds the index of the selected entry (0 = first). An optional statement runs whenever the selection changes, after all dialog variables have been updated.
tools.notes: No array element may be empty: an empty string ends the list there. An initial index outside the array is set to 0.

tools.name: dlgGridLayout
tools.description: Opens a grid layout context in which objects are placed with dlgCell(row, column). Rows and columns are created automatically as needed, so no size has to be declared. Use it for aligned label/field forms.
tools.notes: Only dlgCell may appear directly inside; indexes start at (0, 0) in the upper left.

tools.name: dlgGroup
tools.description: Defines a titled group frame, typically holding radio buttons or check boxes, but any objects are allowed. It contains a dlgVBoxLayout by default. Radio buttons inside one group are numbered from 0 and share one selection variable.
tools.notes: Radio buttons must be placed inside a dlgGroup.

tools.name: dlgHBoxLayout
tools.description: Opens a horizontal box layout context: the contained objects are placed from left to right. Combine it with dlgStretch and dlgSpacing to control the distribution of space, e.g. right-aligned buttons.
tools.notes: Layouts can be nested and mixed with vertical and grid layouts.

tools.name: dlgIntEdit
tools.description: Defines an entry field for an int value bound to a variable and limited to a minimum and maximum. An initial value outside the range is clipped to it.
tools.notes: For a field with up/down arrows use dlgSpinBox; for reals dlgRealEdit.

tools.name: dlgLabel
tools.description: Displays a text label (literal or string variable, HTML allowed, external links open in the associated application). With Update non-zero and a string variable, the label follows later changes to that variable. A hotkey in the text moves the focus to the object defined right after the label.
tools.notes: In HTML texts write < > & for literal characters. Update only makes sense for a dedicated string variable (not a loop variable). If the text contains '&', the next character becomes an Alt hotkey; write \\& in the ULP source for a literal '&'.

tools.name: dlgListBox
tools.description: Defines a single-column list box filled from a string array, with the selected index stored in an int variable. The optional statement runs when the user double-clicks an entry; call dlgSelectionChanged() inside it to also react to simple selection changes.
tools.notes: No element may be empty (the list ends at the first empty string). An initial index outside the array selects nothing.

tools.name: dlgListView
tools.description: Defines a multi-column list with tab-separated column headers and rows taken from a string array of tab-separated values. The user can sort by clicking a header and reorder columns; Selected always refers to the index in the array, and the optional Sort variable sets or returns the sort column (1-based, negative for descending). The statement runs on double-click, or also on selection changes when it calls dlgSelectionChanged().
tools.usage: dlgListView(string Headers, string array[], int &Selected[, int &Sort]) [ statement ]
tools.notes: Selected = -1 means no initial selection, -2 selects the first item in the current sort order; -1 is returned if nothing is selected. Rows must not be empty (the list ends at the first empty string); missing fields are shown empty and extra fields dropped. With an empty Headers string, array[0] is used as header and indexes start at 1. Use a numeric string array for alphanumeric sorting. User sorting does not change the array.

tools.name: dlgPushButton
tools.description: Defines a push button that executes its statement when pressed, after all dialog variables have been updated (changes made in the statement are shown when it returns). A leading '+' makes it the default button (Enter), a leading '-' the cancel button (closing the dialog).
tools.notes: The statement of a '-' cancel button must call dlgReject(), otherwise the user may be unable to close the dialog. Escape a literal leading '+' or '-'. If the text contains '&', the next character becomes an Alt hotkey; write \\& in the ULP source for a literal '&'.

tools.name: dlgRadioButton
tools.description: Defines a radio button inside a dlgGroup; all buttons of the group share one int variable that receives the index (from 0) of the selected button. The initial value selects the initially checked button, and an optional statement runs whenever the button is selected.
tools.notes: Only allowed within a dlgGroup. Set Selected before the first button and do not change it between buttons, otherwise the selection is undefined; a value outside the range selects nothing. If the text contains '&', the next character becomes an Alt hotkey; write \\& in the ULP source for a literal '&'.

tools.name: dlgRealEdit
tools.description: Defines an entry field for a real value bound to a variable and limited to a minimum and maximum. An initial value outside the range is clipped.
tools.notes: Convert entered mm/mil values to internal units with mm2u()/mil2u() before comparing with object members.

tools.name: dlgSpacing
tools.description: Inserts a fixed amount of empty space, in pixels, into a horizontal or vertical box layout.
tools.notes: Use dlgStretch for flexible space.

tools.name: dlgSpinBox
tools.description: Defines an int entry field with up/down arrows bound to a variable and limited to a minimum and maximum. Values outside the range are clipped.
tools.notes: See dlgIntEdit for a plain entry field.

tools.name: dlgStretch
tools.description: Inserts stretchable empty space into a box layout; the factor weights how the free space is shared between several stretch objects. Typical use is pushing buttons to the right or centering a label.
tools.notes: Only meaningful in horizontal or vertical box layouts.

tools.name: dlgStringEdit
tools.description: Defines a one-line text entry field bound to a string variable. With a History array the entries the user made are remembered and offered through a drop-down button (most recent at index 0), optionally limited to Size entries.
tools.notes: History must not contain empty strings (entries after the first empty one are dropped). For multi-line text use dlgTextEdit.

tools.name: dlgTabPage
tools.description: Defines one page of a dlgTabWidget with a title and its content (a dlgVBoxLayout by default). A hotkey in the title opens the page with Alt+key.
tools.notes: Only allowed directly inside a dlgTabWidget. If the text contains '&', the next character becomes an Alt hotkey; write \\& in the ULP source for a literal '&'.

tools.name: dlgTabWidget
tools.description: Container for a set of dlgTabPage objects. The optional int variable selects the initially shown page and is updated when the user switches pages (first page = 0).
tools.notes: Only dlgTabPage objects may appear in the sequence (statements such as for loops that create pages are fine).

tools.name: dlgTextEdit
tools.description: Defines a multi-line text entry field bound to a string variable, with lines separated by '\n'. Trailing whitespace of lines and empty lines at the end are removed when the dialog returns.
tools.notes: Use dlgTextView for read-only (HTML) text.

tools.name: dlgTextView
tools.description: Defines a read-only multi-line text viewer; the text may contain HTML and external links open in the associated application. With a Link variable and a statement, clicking a hyperlink runs the statement with Link set to the href value; if Link is still non-empty afterwards the default link handling follows.
tools.usage:
dlgTextView(string Text)
dlgTextView(string Text, string &Link) statement
tools.notes: When Link is given, external links are not opened automatically. A Link preset before the dialog opens scrolls to that anchor initially.

tools.name: dlgVBoxLayout
tools.description: Opens a vertical box layout context: the contained objects are placed from top to bottom. dlgDialog, dlgGroup and dlgTabPage already contain one by default.
tools.notes: Layouts can be nested to build column structures.

tools.name: Dialog layout (grid, horizontal, vertical)
tools.description: Every dialog object sits in a layout context: a grid layout needs explicit cell coordinates via dlgCell (with optional spans), a horizontal box places objects left to right and a vertical box top to bottom. dlgStretch and dlgSpacing refine the distribution of space in box layouts, and the three kinds can be nested and mixed freely.
tools.notes: dlgDialog, dlgGroup and dlgTabPage default to a vertical box, dlgCell to a horizontal box.

tools.name: dlgAccept
tools.description: Closes the dialog and accepts the user's changes, which are copied into the variables bound to the dialog objects. The optional Result (default 1, normally positive) becomes the return value of dlgDialog(). The dialog closes after the current statement sequence finishes, so statements after dlgAccept() still run.
tools.notes: Use distinct Result values to tell which button closed the dialog.

tools.name: dlgRedisplay
tools.description: Refreshes the dialog immediately with the current values of its variables while program code is still running, e.g. to show a status text before a lengthy operation. It is not needed at the end of a statement, where objects are updated automatically.
tools.notes: A dlgLabel only follows its variable if created with the Update parameter set.

tools.name: dlgReset
tools.description: Resets all objects of the current dialog to their initial values, discarding the user's changes without closing the dialog. dlgReject() implies a reset.
tools.notes: Restores the values the variables had when the dialog was opened.

tools.name: dlgReject
tools.description: Closes the dialog and discards the user's changes: the bound variables get their original values back. The optional Result (default 0, normally 0 or negative) becomes the return value of dlgDialog(). As with dlgAccept(), the statements following the call still run before the dialog closes.
tools.notes: Implies dlgReset(). A '-' cancel button must call it.

tools.name: dlgSelectionChanged
tools.description: Used inside the statement of a dlgListBox or dlgListView to tell whether the statement was called because the selection changed (non-zero) or because of a double-click (zero). Merely containing a call to it makes the statement run on selection changes too, including once for an initial selection when the dialog opens.
tools.notes: Programmatic changes to the list contents or selection do not trigger the statement; update dependent objects yourself.

tools.name: Dialog escape character
tools.description: Some characters have a special meaning in button and label texts ('&' for hotkeys, leading '+'/'-' for default/cancel buttons, leading icon characters in dlgMessageBox). To show such a character literally, prefix it with a backslash in the dialog text, which in ULP source must be written as two backslashes because the parser removes the first one.
tools.usage:
dlgLabel("Miller \\& Co.");       // displays: Miller & Co.
dlgPushButton("\\+10%") ...        // button text starting with a literal '+'
tools.notes: In HTML texts, literal <, > and & are written as <, > and & instead.

tools.name: Complete dialog example
tools.description: A full data-entry dialog combining the layout contexts and the common objects: centered label, two radio button groups, a file name field with a browse button, a grid of labels and OK/Cancel buttons. Use it as a template for ULP front ends.
tools.usage: int Result = dlgDialog("Title") { layouts, objects, buttons calling dlgAccept()/dlgReject() };
tools.notes: Variables bound to objects hold the user's input after dlgAccept(); after dlgReject() they keep their original values.

tools.name: Supported HTML tags
tools.description: EAGLE renders a subset of HTML in dialog texts (dlgLabel, dlgTextView, dlgMessageBox), in #usage texts and in library DESCRIPTION texts. Text counts as HTML if its first line contains a tag; otherwise wrap it in <html>...</html>. Supported are headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, fonts, images, links and a set of character entities.
tools.usage:
Structure: 

 
 
 
Lists:     
     
       
    1.  
       
       
      
Inline:              
Links:         Images: 
Tables:    
Entities:  < > &   ä ö ü Ä Ö Ü ß © ° µ ± "
tools.notes: body bgcolor only works in a dlgTextView. For links to local files with blanks use href="file:/path with blanks/x.html". may also reference an external URL.
